title: The cheap printer's real cost
hook: One printer costs $60, the other $150. Which one costs less in the end?

knows: how to read a price tag
doesNotKnow: that a cheaper purchase price can cost more once the cost of using it is added

objective: The learner can explain that total cost is the price plus the cost of use, and that which printer wins depends on how many pages are printed: A wins below about 1,286 pages, B above.

claims.text: Printer A ($60 plus $0.10 a page) costs $260 for 2,000 pages; Printer B ($150 plus $0.03 a page) costs $210.
For 1,000 pages, A costs $160 and B costs $180.
The two printers cost the same at about 1,286 pages.
Total cost is the purchase price plus the cost of using it, so which option costs less depends on how much it is used.
claims.source: Total cost of ownership = price + (cost per use x uses); the two lines in the model cross once.

claims.text: The lesson is a model: invented prices, a constant cost per page, and no repairs, ink waste or resale value.
claims.source: Assumptions of Demo.tsx; stage chip 'Model: price + cost per page, nothing else'.

recall.question: Kettle X costs $20 and uses $0.50 of power a month. Kettle Y costs $35 and uses $0.20 a month. Over 5 years (60 months), which costs less in total?
recall.why: X: 20 + 0.50 x 60 = $50. Y: 35 + 0.20 x 60 = $47. The dearer kettle wins because the running cost is added to the price.
